editorial.headline: Fishing-Port Construction, Open Nationally and Available in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the making, upkeep and rebuilding of the physical infrastructure that allows a fishing port to work.
editorial.body:
This activity is the construction brief behind a fishing port’s working edge: building, maintaining and rebuilding jetties, trestles and port facilities, along with related infrastructure of the same kind. Its scope also reaches waterways or canals, ports and river-route facilities, docks and locks. In practical terms, it concerns the built systems that make maritime access, berthing and port operations possible—not a narrow single-structure job, but the construction and renewal of the wider port environment described in the classification.

Registration is open across every listed business scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. That matters because the activity is framed as a construction category broad enough to accommodate work at different organisational sizes, while remaining specific about its setting in fishing-port infrastructure. The national position is equally direct. Foreign investment is permitted, and the ceiling on foreign ownership stands at 100%. There is no partial-cap wording in the record to soften or qualify that national opening: a foreign investor may hold the full permitted stake.

Bali does not reverse that result. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for activities assessed as Low or Medium-Low risk, island-wide. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. At the Large scale, its OSS risk classification is Medium-High or High, placing it outside the risk bands caught by the provincial restriction. The Bali position is therefore not a workaround or a conditional reading of a national rule; on the record supplied, the activity remains available for PMA registration in Bali today.

That distinction is worth holding clearly. National openness is not, by itself, a promise that every activity can be registered by PMA in Bali. Here, however, both layers align: the national framework permits up to full foreign ownership, and Bali’s moratorium does not bar this activity because of its stated risk position at the Large scale. For founders considering work on fishing-port buildings and related maritime facilities, the classification offers a clean regulatory starting point: an activity defined by substantial port infrastructure, open across the listed scales, and not blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: Here, both layers align: national rules permit full foreign ownership, and Bali’s moratorium does not bar the activity.
